title: Pressing Abort is drawn as a process crash: rose alert, 'process ended here'
body:
## Summary
The simulated run's Abort lands on `status: "failed"`, and every failed render treats it as a machine crash. RunStage shows a rose `severity="error"` Notice (role=alert) titled "the run did not finish". RunTrace draws a rose "process ended here" row, and RunStatus reads "ended early". The outcome picker was deleted (controls.tsx:15-19; useResearchRun.ts:38-45), so Abort is now the ONLY way a creator can reach `failed`. That means 100% of the failed renders a creator can see are their own click, presented as an engine failure. The hook itself says the opposite: abort fires no bell "because you already know you stopped it" (useEducationalResearch.ts:142-147). The sibling real-run stop (live.ts:262-276) goes silently to idle.

## Description
useResearchRun.ts:171-181 `stop()` writes `{status:"failed", error: STOPPED}`. STOPPED (:35-36) is a good sentence ("Stopped by you at this step. ..."), but it is the body of a Notice whose title and tone say crash. The crash text PROCESS_ERROR (trace.ts:54-55, "claude exited 1 during phase 3 ...") shares every visual with it. RunTrace.tsx:130-147 cannot tell the two apart and always prints "process ended here" in rose. Fix: give the failed variant in types.ts an optional `stoppedByUser?: true` and set it in `stop()`. Branch on it in three places. RunStage renders `<Notice severity="warning" title="stopped">` with STOPPED verbatim and a neutral "run it again". RunTrace's died row reads "stopped here" in white/amber, not rose. statusOf returns `stopped · Ns`. The PROCESS_ERROR path stays rose and unchanged for when a real failure is wired.

## Flow
- Step 1 (guided) → type a topic → Research this → Abort.
- What appears: a rose role=alert box 'the run did not finish', a rose 'process ended here' row, and the status 'ENDED EARLY'. A screen reader interrupts assertively with the error.

## Expected impact
The creator's own action reads as theirs. The rose/alert channel is reserved for real failures, so it keeps its weight when one is eventually wired. The two stop paths (simulated, real) stop disagreeing about what a stop is.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a user-initiated stop must not render with the same title, tone and role as a process failure
Before: reachable failed renders = 1 kind (abort), drawn with 3 crash signals (error Notice role=alert, 'process ended here' rose, 'ended early'); user-stop vs process-death distinguishable only by the body sentence
After: abort renders a warning Notice 'stopped', a 'stopped here' non-rose trace row and 'stopped · Ns'; process failure keeps all 3 crash signals
Method: probe - source ratchet plus a type-level assertion
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/research/run/useResearchRun.ts:35-36 (STOPPED), :38-45 (nothing sets outcome; failed reached by abort), :171-181 (stop -> failed); app/_phases/research/run/controls.tsx:15-19 ('Abort still lands there'), :159-171 ('ended early'); app/_phases/research/guided/RunStage.tsx:315-329 (severity=error, 'the run did not finish'); app/_phases/_shared/ui/Notice.tsx:35 (error -> role=alert); app/_phases/research/run/RunTrace.tsx:130-147 ('process ended here', rose); app/_phases/research/guided/useEducationalResearch.ts:142-147 (abort: no bell, 'you already know you stopped it'); app/_phases/research/run/live.ts:262-276 (real-run stop -> idle)
verify: New probe tests/golden-path/research-abort-not-crash.probe.spec.ts, source ratchets over the stripComments output. (a) useResearchRun.ts: the stop() body sets `stoppedByUser: true`. (b) RunStage.tsx: has a branch on `stoppedByUser` whose Notice severity is not "error". (c) RunTrace.tsx: contains 'stopped here', and the 'process ended here' row is conditional on !stoppedByUser. (d) controls.tsx statusOf: contains 'stopped ·'. All red on HEAD, green after. tests/live/golden-path.live.spec.ts asserts on run-status only as a presence signal (line 169), so check it still passes its assertions by grep. Run npm run typecheck (the RunState union change) and npm test.

title: Two live regions wrap ticking clocks: SR announces every second of a run
body:
## Summary
LiveResult's running card is `role="status"`, which is polite live and non-atomic. It contains `<Elapsed>`, which re-renders every 1000ms (LiveResult.tsx:103-110, :115-123). So a screen reader announces the changing seconds once a second for the whole minutes-long real run. RunStatus is `aria-live="polite"` around `running · Ns` (controls.tsx:182-191), and its text changes on each of the 15 trace steps (useResearchRun.ts:138-147). Its own docstring states the spec: "aria-live because the ENDING is the part a reader must not have to poll for." The ending is the only thing that should be announced.

## Description
A live region announces every text mutation inside it. Elapsed's interval is unconditional for as long as the card is mounted. For a 3-minute real run that is about 180 polite announcements of '41s', '42s'... queued behind whatever the user is actually reading. RunStatus adds 15 more per simulated run, plus the ending. Fix, with no prose added: (1) LiveResult: take `role="status"` off the running container. Put it on a visually-hidden span whose text is static while running ("a real run is running"), and wrap `<Elapsed>` in `aria-hidden`. (2) RunStatus: render the clock part in an `aria-hidden` span. Keep `aria-live="polite"` on a span that holds only the status word (running / complete / ended early), which changes exactly twice per run. The visual output is identical in both cases.

## Flow
- Screen reader on, Step 1 → run this for real → the reader is told the seconds every second until the run lands.
- Simulated run → 15 'running · Ns' announcements before 'complete'.

## Expected impact
For screen-reader users this replaces about 180 interruptions per real run, and 15 per simulated run, with 2 announcements (start and ending). That is the behaviour the docstring already promises.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a live region announces state changes, not a clock
Before: 2 live regions contain a ticking value (LiveResult running card with Elapsed every 1s; RunStatus with secs() per step); polite announcements per 180s real run ≈ 180
After: 0 live regions contain Elapsed or secs(); announcements per run = 2 (status word at start, at end)
Method: probe - source ratchet over the stripped LiveResult.tsx and controls.tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/research/run/LiveResult.tsx:103-110 (setInterval 1000ms), :115-123 (role=status container holding <Elapsed>); app/_phases/research/run/controls.tsx:174-191 (aria-live=polite around statusOf(), docstring: 'the ending is the part a reader must not have to poll for'), :159-171 (secs in every status string); app/_phases/research/run/useResearchRun.ts:138-147 (elapsedMs rewritten each of 15 steps)
verify: New probe tests/golden-path/research-live-region-quiet.probe.spec.ts. Strip comments from LiveResult.tsx and assert that `<Elapsed` appears only inside an element carrying aria-hidden. A simple form: the line containing '<Elapsed' is enclosed by a span with 'aria-hidden'. Also assert that the running branch's role="status" element is not the parent of Elapsed (no '<Elapsed' between that role="status" opening tag and its closing). In controls.tsx, assert that the element carrying aria-live does not call secs( and that a sibling span with aria-hidden does. Red on HEAD, green after. Keep data-testid="run-status" on the outer span; tests/live/golden-path.live.spec.ts reads it. Coordinate with the narration finding below, which edits the same LiveResult running block: land together or sequentially. Run npm test and npm run typecheck.

title: Live notebook points at 'the triage board below', which the guided face lacks
body:
## Summary
The foot of the real-run notebook card reads "saved with this project · the triage board below still reads the saved 2026-08-11 run". LiveResult is mounted only in the guided wizard's RunStage. In that face there is no triage board below it or anywhere else: the board is the expert face, and the guided face's next stage is "the takes". The date is also a string literal that duplicates `NOTEBOOK.researched`, which StandInNote reads.

## Description
grep shows a single importer: RunStage.tsx:29, mounted at :213 and :276. ResearchStep.tsx:293-307 renders GuidedResearch alone when the face is guided; ResearchTriageBoard is mounted only by ExpertBoard (:406). Below LiveResult at RunStage.tsx:276 is the run log card, not a board. The underlying fact is real and is the work: the downstream cards come from the shipped stand-in, not from this notebook. Only the place it points at is wrong. Fix: name what actually reads the stand-in in this face, and read the date from data. For example: `saved with this project · the takes deal from the {NOTEBOOK.researched} stand-in`, with NOTEBOOK imported from ../../_shared/notebook/notebook (as RunStage.tsx:26 does). An alternative is the StandInNote chip shape. Same word count or fewer.

## Flow
- Guided face → run this for real → the notebook lands.
- The card says 'the triage board below'. Below is the run log, and nothing on the page is called a triage board.

## Expected impact
The one sentence on the card that says where this notebook does NOT go points at a real place. The date can no longer drift from the notebook it names.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - copy names a surface that exists on the screen it is rendered on
Before: 1 mount face (guided) x 1 reference to 'triage board below' = 1 false pointer; 1 hardcoded '2026-08-11' in rendered JSX (LiveResult.tsx:231) vs NOTEBOOK.researched (notebook.ts:19)
After: 0 occurrences of 'triage board below' in app/; 0 date literals in LiveResult's JSX; the date comes from NOTEBOOK.researched
Method: probe - grep count plus a source ratchet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/research/run/LiveResult.tsx:230-232 (the copy); grep -rn 'LiveResult' app --include=*.tsx | grep import -> only app/_phases/research/guided/RunStage.tsx:29; app/_phases/research/ResearchStep.tsx:293-307 (guided face = GuidedResearch only), :406 (board only in ExpertBoard); app/_phases/_shared/notebook/notebook.ts:19 (researched: '2026-08-11'); app/_phases/research/guided/RunStage.tsx:110 (StandInNote reads NOTEBOOK.researched)
verify: New probe tests/golden-path/live-notebook-pointer.probe.spec.ts. Strip comments from LiveResult.tsx and assert it does not contain 'triage board below' and does not match /2026-\d\d-\d\d/ (comments are excluded by the strip), and that it references NOTEBOOK.researched. Red on HEAD, green after. `grep -rn "triage board below" app` returns 0 after. Run npm run check:narration and npm run typecheck.

title: Run stage narrates itself three times: a 33-word paragraph, a fake CTA, a title
body:
## Summary
Three rendered strings in this context have the app as their subject, and each one has a sibling that already says it in vocabulary form. (1) The LiveResult running card has a 33-word paragraph: "The engine is writing a notebook about ... This is minutes, not seconds, and it is billing right now — leaving the step does not cancel it, and the bell reports the result." The simulated sibling says the same with a Bell glyph and "in the background — the bell reports the result" (RunStage.tsx:299-307). "minutes, not seconds" restates the Hint on the button that started it (controls.tsx:144-146). (2) RunStage.tsx:357-359 has a non-interactive cyan "Next deals the takes →". It is styled like a link with an arrow, it does nothing, and its subject is the Deck's own button. (3) FaceSwitch's `title={`Switch to ${word}. Nothing is discarded — both faces read and write the same record.`}` (GuidedResearch.tsx:51) is an 86-character native title. It is the only prose template-literal title in app/ and components/, and check:narration's `title="..."` regex (check-narration.mjs:148) cannot see it.

## Description
The work in (1) is the topic, the fact that it is billing, and the elapsed time. The rest is mechanism. Replace the paragraph with the topic as a one-line heading (the work, kept verbatim), an amber `billing` chip (`${CHIP_CLASS} ${TALLY_TONE.amber}`), and the running-note shape copied from RunStage: Bell + "in the background — the bell reports the result". (2) Delete the span. The Deck's Next is the control and is enabled at that moment. (3) Delete the title attribute. The visible label "switch to the guided wizard" is the accessible name, and "nothing is discarded" is reassurance about the app.

## Flow
- A real run starts, and a 33-word paragraph appears under the eyebrow while the simulated run's equivalent is one glyph line.
- A simulated run lands, and a cyan arrow sentence sits where a button would be. Clicking it does nothing.
- Hovering the face switch for about 1s shows a two-sentence tooltip.

## Expected impact
About 50 words of app narration go, the two run paths get one spelling of the background-job fact, and one fake affordance is removed.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - rendered text whose subject is the app goes; the work (topic, billing, elapsed) stays
Before: 3 app-subject strings (LiveResult.tsx:125-128 = 33 words; RunStage.tsx:357-359 = 4 words + arrow, non-interactive cyan; GuidedResearch.tsx:51 = 14-word title); prose template-literal titles in tree = 1 (grep -rnE 'title=\{`[^`]{40,}`\}' -> 3 hits, 2 are data)
After: 0 of the 3; LiveResult running card = eyebrow + topic + billing chip + Bell running-note; prose template-literal titles = 0
Method: probe - source ratchet plus a grep count
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/research/run/LiveResult.tsx:125-128 (paragraph); app/_phases/research/guided/RunStage.tsx:299-307 (sibling Bell running-note), :357-359 ('Next deals the takes ->', a span with no handler); app/_phases/research/run/controls.tsx:144-146 (Hint 'minutes, not milliseconds'); app/_phases/research/guided/GuidedResearch.tsx:51 (template title); pipeline/check-narration.mjs:148 (only matches title="..."); grep -rnE 'title=\{`[^`]{40,}`\}' app components -> 3 hits (VariantContactSheet:150 and ScoreSpotting:774 are data)
verify: New probe tests/golden-path/research-run-no-narration.probe.spec.ts, over stripComments output. It asserts: LiveResult.tsx does not contain 'The engine is writing'; RunStage.tsx does not contain 'Next deals the takes'; GuidedResearch.tsx's FaceSwitch has no 'title=' attribute; LiveResult.tsx contains 'billing' and imports Bell from 'lucide-react'. Red on HEAD, green after. `grep -rn "live-run-running" tests` returns none today; keep the data-testid. Land together with, or after, the live-region finding (same LiveResult running block). Run npm run check:narration, npm run typecheck and npm test, then capture the guided research screen and open the PNG to confirm the running card is not a gap.

title: Run-log phase headings are the dimmest text in the ledger (2.6:1)
body:
## Summary
RunTrace's PhaseHeading docstring is the spec: "with the ledger flattened, the phase is the one thing here that has to out-rank a row" (RunTrace.tsx:58-59). The heading is drawn at text-white/30, which is 2.59:1 on --gt-ink #080a10. Every column of every row is brighter: label slate-200 (16.05:1), detail white/40 (3.77:1), time white/35 (3.14:1), kind at /80 tones. It is bigger, but it is the faintest text in the card apart from the '···' glyph, and it sits under 3:1.

## Description
RunTrace.tsx:60-66 has `text-content tracking-[0.16em] text-white/30 uppercase`. The headings carry PHASE_LABEL, the research prompt's own phases. The comment at :34-36 says they are "the only thing here that says what the process is DOING". Fix: raise to text-white/60 (7.3:1). That out-ranks the white/40 detail column and stays below the slate-200 row label, so a heading reads as a heading and not as a louder row. The row/heading hierarchy then comes from size and tracking plus alpha, instead of size against alpha.

## Flow
- Step 1 (guided) → Research this → the run log grows. The phase headings ('1 · FACTUAL SPINE', '3 · BUILD THE MECHANISMS'...) recede behind the rows they group.

## Expected impact
The one element the ledger's own design says must out-rank a row becomes legible, rising from 2.59:1 to 7.3:1.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the phase heading out-ranks every row column and clears 4.5:1
Before: PhaseHeading white/30 = 2.59:1; row columns 3.14-16.05:1 (heading ranks last of 5)
After: PhaseHeading white/60 = 7.3:1 (ranks above detail/time/kind alpha, below the row label)
Method: probe - source ratchet, plus contrast computed (sRGB relative luminance, white over #080a10)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: app/_phases/research/run/RunTrace.tsx:58-59 (docstring: the phase 'has to out-rank a row'), :60-66 (text-white/30), :95-106 (row columns slate-200 / white/40 / white/35 / kind /80); contrast on #080a10 (app/globals.css:91 --gt-ink): white/30 2.59, /35 3.14, /40 3.77, /60 7.3, slate-200 16.05
verify: New probe tests/golden-path/run-trace-phase-rank.probe.spec.ts. Strip comments from RunTrace.tsx, slice the PhaseHeading function body, and assert it does not contain 'text-white/30' and does contain 'text-white/60'. Red on HEAD, green after. Note: the abort finding above also edits RunTrace.tsx (the died row), so sequence them. Run npm test, then capture the guided research screen mid-run and open the PNG.

lens_checked.visual-craft: Read in full RunTrace, LiveResult, controls, GuidedResearch, RunStage and passes, plus the signal README; checked CHIP_CLASS/TALLY_TONE use in StandInNote and ReasonedNote (correct), the gradient art strips (aria-hidden), the RunTrace row/heading alpha ranking (filed), and the DeckCard chip tones in passes.tsx (the rose-less deck mapping is documented and deliberate).
lens_checked.ux-reviewer: Run start/abort/fail/no-tension/done paths in RunStage; the openedReady compact card; the Deck blockedHint gate; ArtifactPills 'clear the research' (guarded by ClearDialog in ResearchStep.tsx:320, so not a finding); RealRunControl disabled-with-reason; the 'Next deals the takes' fake CTA (filed under copy).
lens_checked.state-coverage: useResearchRun states idle/running/done/no-tension/failed and the live idle/running/done/failed states: abort vs crash render identically (filed); no-tension is unreachable from the UI (documented at useResearchRun.ts:38-45, not a defect); a pre-flight of undefined vs null goes through spendNote (live.ts), and the button is disabled when not serving.
lens_checked.copy-auditor: Hints at RunStage:109-111, controls:144-146 and LiveResult:66-68 (all 12 words or fewer); GuidedResearch blockedHint; the LiveResult foot pointer (filed); the narration sites (filed); one concept, two spellings for background-job + bell (filed with the narration).
lens_checked.accessibility-checker: Live regions (filed); TopicField aria-label; StandInNote sr-only; ReasonedNote sr-only; RunTrace truncated cells keep full text in the DOM; the ArtifactPills buttons lack type=button but are not inside a form (no effect).

lens_no_surface.mobile-specialist: The wizard is desktop-first; RunTrace's fixed 4-column grid is a deliberate ledger. Not judged narrow.
